q: Is moving fuel by pipeline lower carbon than by tanker truck?
title: Fuel by pipeline vs tanker truck
short: Usually yes per tonne-kilometre, because pumps move far more fuel per unit of energy than trucks burning diesel. The pipeline operator counts its pumping power and fuel. A fuel buyer usually finds this transport inside the fuel's upstream emissions, Scope 3 Category 3, unless it pays for transport separately.
audience: Fuel retailers, depots and bulk fuel buyers

ul: Pipeline operator: Scope 2 for pumping electricity, Scope 1 for any fuel burned at stations.
Buyer: Category 3 well-to-tank, or Category 4 if you pay for transport separately.

p: Ask the operator for energy per tonne-kilometre. For trucks, use litres of diesel per trip at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
